Carbon membranes yield highly tortuous paths for CO diffusion, allow the catalytic side reaction associated with hydrogen 2 generation (H ), yield relatively poor electronic conductivity for scaled membranes, yield 2 poor strength for large, self-supporting membranes, and generate relatively large 18 faradaic losses when scaled. Freeze-tape cast membranes can utilize new materials that can combine catalysis, diffusion, and structural support in a single material through a water-based, environmentally clean process, thus supporting a methodology to cleanly and effectively capture and re-utilize carbon dioxide.
